entries.description: Line on a finished objective giving its completion date and time. %1$s is the formatted date and time.
Shown when a wrong exam answer locks the question for a while. %1$s is the time when answering is allowed again.

Hint for an objective task. The value is a URL to the AAPS wiki (English documentation); do not translate the link text, only use a localized wiki URL if the language has one and the path is identical.
Error shown when the trusted current time could not be fetched from the internet when starting or verifying an objective. Fragment, no subject.
Task name in objective 7, completed when max IOB is configured. 'Simple mode' is the simplified user interface setting where the user doesn't set max IOB.
Error shown when starting or verifying an objective needs internet (to read a trusted time) and the phone is offline. Short sentence.

Card title naming the objective by its order number, e.g. '3. Objective'. %1$d is the objective number, starting at 1. Objectives are the sequential learning steps a user must pass before AAPS enables closed-loop features.
Reason shown when a loop feature is blocked because the objective was started but not completed. %1$d is the objective number.
Reason shown when a loop feature is blocked because an earlier objective was never started. %1$d is the objective number.
Requirement text of objective 1, i.e. what must be done to pass it. BG is blood glucose; Nightscout is a web service for monitoring.
Lesson shown after objective 1 is completed. Full sentences. Nightscout is a product name; AAPS is the app (Android Artificial Pancreas System).
Description of objective 1: what the user is learning. Noun phrase shown as the objective's headline text. 'Basals' and 'ratios' are insulin delivery settings (basal rates, insulin-to-carb ratios).
Requirement text of objective 10: read the docs and set up simple automation rules.
Lesson shown after objective 10 is completed, a warning not to overuse automation.
Description of objective 10: enabling Automation (rule-based actions in AAPS).
Requirement text of objective 8. 'Looping' means running AAPS in closed loop; 'carb entry' means entering eaten carbohydrates.
Lesson shown after objective 8 is completed. Autosens result is a percentage around 100% when the profile fits.
Description of objective 8: adjusting basals and ratios, then enabling autosens (automatic sensitivity detection).
Task name in objective 1: glucose readings must show up in Nightscout or Tidepool (online services). Fragment, appears as a checklist line.
Short imperative on the button that starts the next objective, which begins its timer and tasks.
Short imperative on the button that checks whether the objective's tasks are done, or in the exam whether the selected answers are correct.
Short toggle label to collapse the list of lessons of a completed objective. Opposite of the 'More' label.
Accessibility/marker text for an answer option that is the correct one, shown after the question is answered. Lower case fragment.
Requirement text of objective 3: study the questions; each has four answers and possibly several are correct.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about reviewing the profile (basal and ratios) for better results. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, that carbohydrates can only be entered in grams. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about COB (carbs on board) calculation depending on the ISF/IC relation. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about converting from U200 insulin with a 50% profile when using the insulin concentration feature. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about switching from U200 with a 50% profile to the insulin concentration feature. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about when insulin concentration can be changed (only when insulin or patch is changed). Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about DIA (duration of insulin action) having a different meaning in looping than in classic pump therapy. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about e-carbs (extended carbs) as a replacement for extended bolus. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about reducing insulin before exercise by choosing a profile switch below 100%. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about setting a higher temporary target before exercise. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about the hypo temp target (temporary higher glucose target after a low). Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about IC (insulin-to-carb ratio) and how it determines insulin to cover carbs. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about setting the correct insulin type because it affects IOB calculation. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about using the IOB (insulin on board) graph to analyze how well AAPS works. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about ISF (insulin sensitivity factor, glucose drop per unit of insulin) and how it drives correction doses. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about not looping unattended when CGM (continuous glucose monitor) values are unreliable. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about remote monitoring and control via Nightscout and its limits. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about backing up the progress of objectives together with settings. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about keeping exported settings and the APK outside the phone. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about what the user needs to pass the objectives (Nightscout, a compatible pump, a computer to build AAPS). Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, that AAPS can run offline. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about using percentage in a profile switch, which scales basal, ISF and IC but not targets. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, that editing a profile requires a profile switch to take effect. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about timeshift in a profile switch to adapt the daily profile to a shifted schedule. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, that AAPS must know when the pump is disconnected to compute IOB correctly. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about sensitivity detection (autosens) in the algorithm. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Lesson shown after passing a matching exam question, about resolving wrong carb entries quickly to avoid overdosing. Full sentence(s) for the user.
Short navigation button to the next exam question.
Short navigation button that jumps to the next question not yet answered.
Description of objective 3: a quiz about AAPS knowledge.
Short navigation button to the previous exam question.
Progress counter above an exam question. %1$d is the current question number, %2$d the total number of questions.
Short button that clears the selected answers of the current exam question.
Short toggle label to expand the list of lessons of a completed objective. Opposite of the 'Less' label.
No usage found in code.
Task name in objective 4: the user must manually enact (apply) a number of temp basals suggested by the open loop. Short checklist line.
Task name in objective 5; completed when the user acts on the loop's recommendation. Imperative sentence.
Requirement text of objective 5: the user decides the max basal value. 'Max basal' is the upper limit on temporary basal rate; 'simple terms' introduces a rule of thumb.
Lesson shown after objective 5 is completed, about safety limits.
Description of objective 5: understanding the open loop's temp basal recommendations.
Requirement text of objective 7. BG = blood glucose; 'low BG alarms' are alarms for low glucose.
Lesson shown after objective 7 is completed, about keeping max IOB appropriate. 'Food' means carbohydrate boluses.
Description of objective 7: tuning the closed loop by raising max IOB above 0 and lowering BG targets step by step.
Requirement text of objective 6. 'Max IOB' is the maximum insulin on board allowed; here it is forced to 0.
Lesson shown after objective 6 is completed. IOB = insulin on board; basal rate = background insulin.
Description of objective 6: closing the loop with Low Glucose Suspend (LGS), where the pump only reduces insulin to prevent lows.
Empty-state text when an objective has no lessons to show.
No usage found in code.
Requirement text of objective 4. Temp basal = temporary basal rate; 'default temp targets' are preset temporary glucose targets.
Lesson shown after objective 4 is completed, about when open loop is appropriate.
Description of objective 4: running in open loop, i.e. AAPS only suggests temp basals and the user enacts them manually.
Task name in objective 1: pump status must be visible in Nightscout or Tidepool. Fragment, checklist line.
Short label of the button revealing a hint (a link to the AAPS documentation) for a task.
Requirement text of objective 9. maxIOB is the max insulin on board setting; SMB are small automatic boluses; 'meal bolus' is the bolus for food.
Lesson shown after objective 9 is completed. Oref1 is the name of the algorithm.
Description of objective 9: enabling SMB (super micro bolus) and other daytime features.
Short state chip: objective is completed.
Short state chip: objective was started and is not finished.
Short state chip: objective cannot be started until the previous ones are completed.
Short state chip: objective can be started now but has not been yet.
Requirement text of objective 2: perform the listed actions in the app.
Lesson shown after objective 2 is completed. 'Overview' is the name of the main screen; click and long click are touch gestures.
Description of objective 2: learning how to control AAPS.
Task name in objective 2: use the 'disconnect pump' action for one hour, as when showering. Imperative.
Task name in objective 2: open the Loop plugin's screen. Imperative.
Task name in objective 2: perform a profile switch at 90% for 10 minutes. A profile switch temporarily scales basal and sensitivity settings. Imperative.
Task name in objective 2, follows the disconnect task: reconnect the pump the same way. Starts with an ellipsis to continue the previous line.
Task name in objective 2: scroll or zoom the glucose chart on the main screen. Imperative.
Task name in objective 2: create a custom temporary glucose target lasting 10 minutes. Imperative.
No usage found in code.
Error shown on Verify when the objective's tasks are not all completed yet.
No usage found in code.

Hint for an objective task. The value is a URL to the AAPS wiki (English documentation); do not translate the link text, only use a localized wiki URL if the language has one and the path is identical.

Hint for an objective task. The value is a URL to the AAPS wiki (English documentation); do not translate the link text, only use a localized wiki URL if the language has one and the path is identical.
Task name in objective 1: the user must confirm they know the master password, which protects exported settings. Imperative.
Heading above the list of lessons the user has learned from an objective. Ends with a colon.
Short feedback after the user submits a wrong answer in an objective exam.
